**Key observations from the test image:**
- Tomato leaf affected
- Numerous small, dark brown/black spots (specks) scattered across the entire leaf surface
- Yellow/chlorotic halos surrounding many of the dark spots
- Brown necrotic leaf margins
- No bullseye/concentric ring patterns (rules out Early Blight)
- No large water-soaked lesions (rules out Late Blight)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- No wilting symptoms (rules out Bacterial Wilt/Verticillium Wilt)
- No mosaic/mottling (rules out Cucumber Mosaic Virus)

The pattern of numerous tiny dark specks with surrounding yellow chlorotic halos is the hallmark of **Bacterial Speck of Tomato** (*Pseudomonas syringae* pv. *tomato*), distinguishable from Septoria Leaf Blotch (which has larger spots with defined lighter centers) and Early Blight (which has concentric ring bullseye lesions).
